notes: Scope of verification: every number in siteThickness/regressions/partition/bodyFatPercent was read from an opened full text, supplementary appendix or official table, except entries explicitly flagged derived:true (computed here from published points, which are listed) and ratio_ofMedians / implied values described in notes. Sources with access 'read-about' contribute no numbers.
Schema deviations: sex may be 'both' where the source pooled sexes; some rows carry sem_mm (standard error) instead of sd_mm; extra fields median_mm and percentiles_mm are added where available.

No single open source stratifies SAT thickness by BOTH sex and BMI at all body sites. Sex x BMI cells exist only for arm, anterior thigh and abdomen (Jain 2013, very small n) and via regression with a sex term for abdomen and arm (Sim 2014) and deltoid (Kowatari 2023, Sebro 2022). Buttock has BMI classes OR sex, never both. Forearm, calf, lateral thigh, back and flank have men-only segment means (Storchle 2018, n=10) plus one female athlete (Muller 2016).

Most injection-site data come from adults with diabetes aged ~50-65; insulin users may have lipohypertrophy at injection sites. Values for 20-year-old students are probably somewhat lower in the abdomen (Gibney: abdomen SAT 10.3 mm at 18-39 y vs 14.3-14.8 mm at 40+), similar in thigh/arm/buttock.

Ultrasound values are uncompressed single-layer SAT (skin excluded unless includesSkin is true). Skinfold values are a compressed double layer of skin + fat and are recorded raw; do not mix the two without a conversion model.

Ethnicity: at the same BMI, Asian subjects in Gibney 2010 had thicker abdominal SAT (15.2 vs 12.2 mm in Whites) but thinner arm/thigh/buttock SAT, and Chinese women had a higher VAT/SAT ratio than BMI-matched Caucasians (Kalimeri 2021). Asian BMI cut-offs (23 / 25 or 24 / 28 in mainland China) differ from WHO (25 / 30); class labels are kept exactly as each paper defined them.

Sexual dimorphism summary supported by the data: women have roughly 1.6x arm, 1.9x thigh, 1.3x abdomen and 1.45x buttock SAT thickness of men (Gibney Table 2 means, BMI pooled); elite female athletes have about 3x the 8-site SAT sum of male athletes (Muller 2020); men have about twice the VAT and a VAT/SAT ratio about 2x that of women (Chiyanika 2021, Linge 2018); android/gynoid fat ratio ~0.4-0.5 in young men vs ~0.3 in young women (Ofenheimer 2020, Staynor 2020).

Saturation: buttock SAT rises little with BMI in Gibney (13.7 -> 15.7 -> 16.6 mm) while abdomen nearly doubles; visceral fat in Chinese men plateaus between overweight and obese without fatty liver (2.61 -> 2.43 L) while abdominal SAT keeps rising.

Known data-quality flags: Liu 2018 male triceps skinfold looks implausibly high; Tai 2026 regression coefficients have unclear units; Ozen 2019 reports SEM and has inconsistent sex counts; Jain 2013 and Sim 2014 values were transcribed from table images.
